title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 5 — Environmental Studies | Plants Animals Around Us
description: Subject-wise test on Plants Animals Around Us (Environmental Studies) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 5. 40Q.
subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which part of a plant usually grows under the ground and absorbs water?

options.explanation: Leaves are primarily involved in photosynthesis, not water absorption.
Stems support the plant and transport water but do not absorb it directly from the soil.
Roots grow underground and absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
Flowers are reproductive parts and do not absorb water.

questions.explanation: Roots are specialized structures that anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients from the soil, growing underground.
questions.hint: This part is responsible for anchoring the plant and absorbing water.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of the following animals is known for building a nest to lay its eggs?

options.explanation: Dogs do not build nests; they give birth to live young.
Fish lay eggs in water but do not build nests.
Birds build nests to lay eggs and protect their young.
Lions do not build nests; they give birth to live young.

questions.explanation: Birds construct nests, typically in trees or on cliffs, to lay eggs and raise their young.
questions.hint: This animal is known for its ability to build structures for its offspring.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: From which part of a plant do we primarily get fruits?

options.explanation: Stems support the plant and transport nutrients but do not produce fruits.
Roots absorb water and nutrients but do not produce fruits.
Leaves perform photosynthesis but do not produce fruits.
Flowers develop into fruits after pollination.

questions.explanation: Flowers are the reproductive parts of plants, and they develop into fruits after pollination.
questions.hint: This part is involved in the reproductive process of the plant.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of these animals is an amphibian, meaning it can live both on land and in water?

options.explanation: Dolphins are mammals and live exclusively in water.
Frogs are amphibians and can live both on land and in water.
Snakes are reptiles and live primarily on land.
Squirrels are mammals and live exclusively on land.

questions.explanation: Frogs are amphibians, characterized by their ability to live both on land and in water during different stages of their life cycle.
questions.hint: This animal can survive in both aquatic and terrestrial environments.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: A cow eats grass and plants. Based on its food habits, a cow is classified as a:

options.explanation: Carnivores eat meat, not plants.
Herbivores eat plants, and cows primarily consume grass and plants.
Omnivores eat both plants and meat.
Scavengers feed on dead animals or decaying matter.

questions.explanation: Herbivores are animals that primarily feed on plants, and a cow is a classic example of a herbivore.
questions.hint: This classification is based on the type of food the animal consumes.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Assertion (A): Plants are called producers in an ecosystem. Reason (R): Plants can make their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Plants are producers because they make their own food through photosynthesis, as explained in the reason.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason correctly explains it.

questions.explanation: Plants are indeed producers because they perform photosynthesis, a process where they create their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide, as stated in the reason.
questions.hint: The reason correctly explains why the assertion is true.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which type of plant has a soft, green stem and usually lives for only one or two seasons?

options.explanation: Trees have woody stems and live for many years.
Herbs have soft, green stems and typically live for one or two seasons.
Shrubs have woody stems and live for multiple years.
Creepers spread on the ground but may have woody or soft stems.

questions.explanation: Herbs are small plants with soft, green, and non-woody stems, typically having a short lifespan.
questions.hint: This type of plant has a soft stem and a short life cycle.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: A camel has a hump on its back and can go without water for many days. This adaptation primarily helps it to:

options.explanation: The hump does not aid in speed.
The hump does not help in hiding.
The hump stores fat, which is metabolized to produce water and energy, aiding survival in arid conditions.
Camels carry loads with their bodies, not specifically the hump.

questions.explanation: The hump on a camel stores fat, which can be metabolized to produce water and energy, allowing it to survive long periods without drinking in arid desert conditions.
questions.hint: This adaptation is crucial for survival in dry environments.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Rina saw a plant that was much shorter than a tree, had several woody branches growing from near the ground, and did not need any support to stand upright. What kind of plant did she observe?

options.explanation: Herbs have soft stems and are usually very short.
Shrubs have woody stems, are shorter than trees, and have multiple branches near the ground.
Creepers spread on the ground and do not stand upright.
Trees are taller and have a single main trunk.

questions.explanation: Shrubs are woody plants that are smaller than trees, typically having multiple stems branching out from or near the ground, unlike herbs (soft stems), creepers (spread on ground), or trees (single main trunk).
questions.hint: This plant has woody branches and is shorter than a tree.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: If a large number of trees are cut down in a forest, what would be the most significant immediate impact on the animals living there?

options.text: Increase in the amount of rainfall.
options.explanation: Cutting trees does not directly increase rainfall.

options.text: More sunlight available for ground plants.
options.explanation: While sunlight may increase, the primary impact is on animals, not plants.

options.text: Loss of habitat and food sources.
options.explanation: Animals lose their homes and food sources when trees are cut down.
Cutting trees would likely increase air pollution due to reduced oxygen production.

questions.explanation: Trees provide shelter (habitat) and food (leaves, fruits, seeds) for a vast number of animals. Cutting them down directly leads to the destruction of these essential resources, forcing animals to relocate or face survival challenges.
questions.hint: Consider the role of trees in providing resources for animals.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of the following is a domestic animal primarily kept for milk?

options.explanation: Tigers are wild animals and not domesticated for milk production.
Foxes are wild animals and not kept for milk.
Cows are domesticated animals primarily kept for milk production.
Elephants are wild animals and not domesticated for milk.

questions.explanation: Cows are commonly domesticated and raised for their milk, which is a staple food product.
questions.hint: This animal is known for providing a white liquid commonly consumed by humans.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: What do plants absorb from the soil through their roots to grow?

options.explanation: Sunlight and air are absorbed by leaves, not roots.
Roots absorb water and mineral nutrients from the soil.
These gases are absorbed through leaves, not roots.
Leaves and flowers are parts of the plant, not absorbed from the soil.

questions.explanation: Roots are specialized to absorb water and essential mineral nutrients from the soil, which are vital for plant growth.
questions.hint: Plants need two key things from the soil to grow properly.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which gas do plants release into the atmosphere during photosynthesis, which is essential for animals and humans to breathe?

options.explanation: Plants absorb carbon dioxide, not release it.
Nitrogen is not directly released by plants during photosynthesis.
Plants release oxygen during photosynthesis, which is essential for respiration.
Methane is not a byproduct of photosynthesis.

questions.explanation: During the process of photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a byproduct.
questions.hint: This gas is what humans and animals inhale to survive.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a food item that we get directly from plants?

options.explanation: Honey is produced by bees, not directly from plants.
Eggs come from birds, not directly from plants.
Wheat is a plant-based food item.
Meat comes from animals, not directly from plants.

questions.explanation: Wheat is a grain that grows on plants and is a direct plant-based food source. Honey comes from bees, eggs from birds, and meat from animals.
questions.hint: This food item is a staple grain used to make bread.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: A farmer observes that the soil in his field is becoming more fertile and has better aeration (more air pockets). Which tiny creatures are most likely helping him achieve this naturally?

options.explanation: Mosquitoes do not contribute to soil fertility or aeration.
Butterflies do not improve soil quality.
Earthworms improve soil fertility and aeration through their burrowing and waste.
Spiders do not contribute to soil health.

questions.explanation: Earthworms burrow through the soil, creating tunnels that improve aeration and drainage. Their waste also enriches the soil, making it more fertile.
questions.hint: These creatures are often called 'nature's ploughmen' for their role in soil health.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: How can you best distinguish a 'shrub' from a 'tree'?

options.text: A shrub is always taller than a tree.
options.explanation: This is not a reliable distinguishing feature.

options.text: A shrub has a thick, single woody stem, while a tree has many thin stems.
options.explanation: This describes a tree, not a shrub.

options.text: A shrub is generally smaller and has many branches growing from near the ground, while a tree has a single main woody stem.
options.explanation: This is the correct structural difference between shrubs and trees.

options.text: Shrubs only bear flowers, whereas trees only bear fruits.
options.explanation: Both shrubs and trees can bear flowers and fruits.

questions.explanation: This describes the primary structural difference: trees have a distinct trunk, while shrubs branch out closer to the ground.
questions.hint: Think about the height and structure of the plant.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Animals like deer, rabbits, and elephants are known as herbivores. What does this mean about their diet?

options.explanation: Herbivores do not eat meat.
Herbivores primarily consume plant-based food.

options.text: They eat both plants and meat.
options.explanation: Herbivores do not eat meat.
Herbivores do not eat insects.

questions.explanation: Herbivores are animals whose diet consists primarily of plants.
questions.hint: Herbivores do not eat meat.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: If a large number of trees are cut down in a forest (deforestation), what is the most immediate negative impact on the local environment?

options.explanation: Deforestation reduces oxygen production.
Deforestation can lead to an increase in temperature.

options.text: Loss of natural habitat for many animals.
options.explanation: Deforestation destroys habitats, leading to loss of animal homes.
Deforestation can reduce rainfall in the long term.

questions.explanation: Forests provide homes, food, and shelter for countless species. Deforestation directly destroys these habitats, leading to the displacement or extinction of animals.
questions.hint: Think about the role of trees in providing shelter and food for animals.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** Plants are often called the 'lungs of the Earth.' **Reason (R):** Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and release oxygen, which is vital for life.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion and reason are both correct, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because plants produce oxygen, similar to how lungs function. The reason correctly explains this role by detailing the gas exchange process.
questions.hint: Consider the function of lungs in humans and compare it to the role of plants.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Priya observes a plant in her garden that has a very weak stem and cannot stand upright on its own. It uses tendrils to wrap around a nearby wall and grow upwards. What type of plant is Priya observing?

options.explanation: Trees have strong, woody stems and do not need support to stand upright.
Shrubs have multiple woody stems and do not typically use tendrils.
Herbs usually have non-woody stems and do not use tendrils to climb.
Climbers have weak stems and use tendrils or other structures to climb.

questions.explanation: Climbers are characterized by their weak stems and their ability to use special structures like tendrils to climb and seek support from other plants or structures.
questions.hint: This type of plant needs support to grow upright.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which part of a plant absorbs water and nutrients from the soil?

options.explanation: Leaves are primarily responsible for photosynthesis, not absorption of water and nutrients.
Flowers are reproductive parts of a plant and do not absorb water or nutrients.
Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
Stems support the plant and transport water and nutrients but do not absorb them directly from the soil.

questions.explanation: Roots are specialized structures that grow into the soil to anchor the plant and absorb essential water and dissolved minerals needed for growth.
questions.hint: This part is usually found underground.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Animals that eat only plants or plant products are known as:

options.explanation: Herbivores eat only plants.
Carnivores eat only meat.
Omnivores eat both plants and meat.
Scavengers feed on dead animals or plant material.

questions.explanation: Herbivores are a type of animal whose diet consists entirely of plant matter, such as grass, leaves, fruits, and seeds.
questions.hint: Think of animals like cows or deer.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of the following products do we get from plants?

options.explanation: Eggs come from animals like chickens.
Milk comes from mammals like cows.
Wood is obtained from trees.
Meat comes from animals.

questions.explanation: Wood is obtained from the trunks and branches of trees, which are plants, and is widely used for construction, furniture, and fuel.
questions.hint: Think of materials derived from trees.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of these animals is primarily adapted to live in water?

options.explanation: Tigers live on land.
Monkeys live on trees and land.
Fish live in water.
Elephants live on land.

questions.explanation: Fish are aquatic animals that possess gills for breathing underwater and fins for movement, making them well-suited for an aquatic environment.
questions.hint: This animal lives and breathes underwater.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Plants release oxygen into the atmosphere, which animals breathe. In return, what do animals release that plants need for photosynthesis?

options.explanation: Water vapour is released during respiration but is not used by plants for photosynthesis.
Nitrogen is a gas present in the atmosphere but not primarily released by animals.
Animals release carbon dioxide, which plants use for photosynthesis.
Methane is released by some animals but is not used by plants for photosynthesis.

questions.explanation: Animals exhale carbon dioxide as a waste product of respiration, and plants absorb this carbon dioxide from the air to use in the process of photosynthesis to make their food.
questions.hint: This gas is a byproduct of animal respiration.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: A plant that has a weak stem and spreads along the ground, rather than growing upwards, is called a:

options.explanation: Trees have strong, upright stems.
Shrubs have woody stems and grow upright.
Climbers have weak stems but grow upwards using support.
Creepers spread along the ground.

questions.explanation: Creepers are plants with weak stems that cannot stand upright and therefore spread horizontally along the ground (e.g., pumpkin, watermelon).
questions.hint: This type of plant grows flat on the ground.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of the following animals lays eggs to reproduce?

options.explanation: Cows give birth to live young.
Dogs give birth to live young.
Hens lay eggs.
Cats give birth to live young.

questions.explanation: Hens are birds, and birds reproduce by laying eggs from which their young hatch, unlike mammals like cows, dogs, and cats which give birth to live young.
questions.hint: This animal is a bird.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Cutting down a large number of trees in a forest can lead to an increase in:

options.explanation: Cutting down trees reduces oxygen production.
Removing trees exposes soil to erosion.
Rainfall is not directly affected by tree removal.
Groundwater levels may decrease due to reduced water retention.

questions.explanation: Tree roots help to bind soil particles together. When trees are removed, the soil becomes exposed and loose, making it more susceptible to being washed away by rain or blown away by wind, leading to increased soil erosion.
questions.hint: This process involves the loss of soil due to wind or water.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Reena observes a plant in her backyard that is much smaller than a tree, has many branches growing from near the ground, and its stem is woody and hard. Which type of plant is Reena most likely observing?

options.explanation: Herbs have soft stems and are usually smaller.
Shrubs have woody stems and multiple branches near the ground.
Creepers spread along the ground and have weak stems.
Trees are much larger and have a single woody stem.

questions.explanation: Shrubs are woody plants that are smaller than trees and typically have multiple stems or branches originating from or near the ground, differentiating them from single-stemmed trees or soft-stemmed herbs and creepers.
questions.hint: This plant is smaller than a tree and has multiple woody stems.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-flowering plant that reproduces through spores?

options.explanation: Mango trees produce flowers and seeds, not spores.
Ferns reproduce through spores and do not produce flowers.
Sunflowers produce flowers and seeds.
Tulsi is a flowering plant that produces seeds.

questions.explanation: Ferns are non-flowering plants that reproduce using spores instead of seeds, unlike mango trees, sunflowers, or tulsi.
questions.hint: Look for plants that do not produce flowers or seeds.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: In the food chain: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Eagle, which organism is the primary consumer?

options.explanation: Grass is a producer, not a consumer.
Grasshopper eats grass, making it the primary consumer.
Frog eats grasshopper, making it a secondary consumer.
Eagle is a tertiary consumer in this food chain.

questions.explanation: The primary consumer is the organism that eats the producer (grass). Here, the grasshopper eats grass, making it the primary consumer.
questions.hint: Primary consumers eat producers like plants.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which animal has a beak adapted for cracking nuts?

options.explanation: Crows have general-purpose beaks, not specialized for cracking nuts.
Parrots have strong beaks adapted for cracking nuts.
Sparrows have small beaks suited for seeds, not nuts.
Pigeons have soft beaks, not adapted for cracking nuts.

questions.explanation: Parrots have strong, curved beaks specifically adapted for cracking and eating nuts and seeds.
questions.hint: Look for birds known for eating hard seeds or nuts.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Assertion (A): Cactus plants store water in their thick stems. Reason (R): Cactus plants grow in deserts where water is scarce. Which option is correct?

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and R correctly explains why cacti store water in their stems.

options.explanation: R correctly explains A, so this option is incorrect.

questions.question: Which plant can a farmer grow around the field to naturally repel pests?

options.explanation: Rice is a crop and does not repel pests.
Marigold plants repel pests naturally.
Wheat is a crop and does not repel pests.
Sugarcane is a crop and does not repel pests.

questions.explanation: Marigold plants release a scent that repels many pests, making them useful as natural pest controllers in farms.
questions.hint: Look for plants known for their pest-repelling properties.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of mammals?

options.explanation: Mammals do not lay eggs (except monotremes, which are rare).
Feathers are a feature of birds, not mammals.
Mammals produce milk to feed their young.
Gills are a feature of fish, not mammals.

questions.explanation: Mammals are warm-blooded animals that feed their young with milk, unlike birds (feathers), reptiles (eggs), or fish (gills).
questions.hint: Look for a feature unique to mammals.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: During a school trip to a forest, Ravi observed that some trees had needle-like leaves and remained green throughout the year. Which type of trees did Ravi most likely observe?

options.explanation: Deciduous trees shed their leaves seasonally and do not have needle-like leaves.
Evergreen trees remain green year-round and can have needle-like leaves.
Coniferous trees are a type of evergreen tree with needle-like leaves.
While both B and C are correct, the question asks for the most likely type, which is coniferous trees (C).

questions.explanation: Needle-like leaves and year-round greenery are typical of evergreen trees, particularly conifers like pine or fir. Both options B and C are correct, but C (coniferous) is more specific.
questions.hint: Evergreen trees with needle-like leaves are usually coniferous.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of these animals undergoes complete metamorphosis in its life cycle?

options.explanation: Frogs undergo incomplete metamorphosis (tadpole to adult).
Cockroaches undergo incomplete metamorphosis.
Butterflies undergo complete metamorphosis.
Earthworms do not undergo metamorphosis.

questions.explanation: Butterflies undergo complete metamorphosis (egg → larva → pupa → adult), unlike frogs (incomplete metamorphosis) or earthworms (no metamorphosis).
questions.hint: Complete metamorphosis involves four distinct stages.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: A seedling bends towards the light. What is this movement called?

options.explanation: Hydrotropism is a response to water.
Geotropism is a response to gravity.
Phototropism is the response to light.
Thigmotropism is a response to touch.

questions.explanation: Phototropism is the growth movement of plants in response to light, causing the seedling to bend towards the window.
questions.hint: This movement is a response to light.
questions.subject: maha5-evs

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of roots in plants?

options.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil.

options.text: Anchoring the plant in the soil
options.explanation: Roots anchor the plant firmly in the soil.
Photosynthesis occurs in leaves, not roots.
Roots store food and nutrients for the plant.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs in the leaves (using sunlight), not roots. Roots primarily absorb water, anchor plants, and store food.
questions.hint: Roots do not produce food; leaves do.
questions.subject: maha5-evs
